channel.title: Hastings Daily
channel.description: Local news for Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill and Battle, three times a day.

item.title: Pilot Field power works to finish by early December, MP says
item.description: UK Power Networks has been working on an underground electrical main in the Pilot Field area of Hastings, and the works have caused a number of power cuts and noisy temporary generators in the neighbourhood in recent months.

item.title: Conquest Hospital Radio wins King's Award
item.description: Conquest Hospital Radio, the volunteer-run station that has been bringing music and company into hospitals in Hastings and the Rother for more than 50 years, has received a King's Award, the highest recognition given to voluntary organisations in the UK.

item.title: Police appeal after two 'deliberate' vehicle fires in Bewbush
item.description: Sussex Police are appealing for witnesses after two vehicle fires in Bewbush, which are being treated as deliberate.

item.title: HMS Prince of Wales spotted off the Hastings coast
item.description: Royal Navy aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales passed the Hastings coast on the morning of Monday 16 November, according to local photographer Marie Richardson, who captured the picture.

item.title: Planning round-up: HMO proposals in St Leonards among latest applications
item.description: A series of planning applications have been submitted to Hastings Borough Council, including proposals for three houses in multiple occupation in St Leonards, according to a round-up of applications published by the Hastings Observer.

item.title: Bexhill GP surgery closed today over 'unforeseen circumstances'
item.description: Sidley Medical Practice, the Bexhill GP surgery on Turkey Road and Albert Road, is closed today. The practice said on its website that "due to some unforeseen circumstances we are unable to operate from our building today".

item.title: Bexhill man launches Taskmarket jobs app after Tourette's ends wedding career
item.description: Luke Jones, 38, from Bexhill, spent more than ten years filming and photographing weddings through his company, Bexhill Film Company. Then in February 2024, at the age of 35, he was diagnosed with Tourette's syndrome, and a job where he had to be in the room all day became impossible, he said.

item.title: Eco-arts magazine Earthworks launches at Hastings Museum
item.description: A new eco-arts magazine is launching in Hastings on the same day the town's museum opens its new environmentally themed exhibition.

item.title: Minor Dents, with Hastings-born Holly Finch, play the Jenny Lind
item.description: A psychedelic rock trio fronted by a Hastings-born singer plays a free gig at the Jenny Lind in December for the last Adventures in Pop! music evening of the year.

item.title: The 1828 battle over smuggled goods at Sidley Green
item.description: A new BBC feature looks back at the night in 1828 when a chase for smuggled goods turned into one of East Sussex's most dramatic confrontations in the fields around Sidley, the village that long ago became part of suburban Bexhill.

item.title: Steyning second-half surge sinks Hastings United 4-1
item.description: Hastings United suffered a heavy defeat on a cold Saturday afternoon at The Pilot Field, where Steyning Town produced a second-half comeback to win 4-1 in the Isthmian South East division in front of a crowd of 1,034.

item.title: Hastings MP says £1.27 million secured for local playgrounds
item.description: Hastings MP Helena Dollimore has said the town will receive £1.27 million to upgrade its playgrounds.

item.title: Police appeal to identify man found on Rottingdean beach
item.description: Police have appealed for help to identify a man found dead on Rottingdean beach in October, who is still unknown.

item.title: East Sussex joins national programme to use creative activities for health
item.description: East Sussex County Council has been selected to join a national programme that uses creative and cultural activities to improve health and wellbeing.

item.title: On this day, 1865: A 70-foot whale stranded at Pevensey goes on sale
item.description: On 15 November 1865, the carcass of a finback whale some 70 feet long was sold by public auction on the shingle at Pevensey, after it washed up at Norman's Bay two days earlier. A coastguard at the Pevensey Sluice Station spotted the dead animal floating in the water on the evening of Monday 13 November, and it came ashore that night.

item.title: Trains between Bexhill and Eastbourne cut short by signalling fault
item.description: Southern services between Bexhill and Eastbourne have been disrupted by a signalling fault, The Argus has reported.

item.title: Sussex Police warn against uninsured drivers with roadside checks
item.description: Sussex Police have warned motorists against uninsured driving, with officers carrying out roadside checks this week in the Eastbourne and Wealden area.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: The council's budget consultation has now opened and runs until 5pm on 16 December. People can take part via an online survey, by email to consultations@rother.gov.uk, or by post to the council's Town Hall in Bexhill. The council said it wants to understand the effect of the proposals before making final budget decisions.

item.title: Nova '78 documentary screens at the Electric Palace
item.description: An 80-minute documentary about the Nova Convention in 1978 New York is coming to Hastings this weekend.

item.title: Shoplifter jailed for thefts across Sussex after £31,000 spree
item.description: Brendan Brain, 39, of Waterlooville, Hampshire, has been jailed for a spree of shoplifting and burglary that stretched across Sussex and ten other counties, Sussex Police said.

item.title: Bexhill community hub to get more than £500,000 in developer funding
item.description: More than £500,000 has been allocated to create a new community hub in Bexhill town centre, Rother District Council said.

item.title: Rye bonfire procession starts at 7pm on Saturday night
item.description: Rye holds its annual bonfire celebrations on Saturday, with a torchlit procession starting at 7pm, according to a guide published by the local press.

item.title: Bexhill county councillor leaves Reform UK to join Conservatives
item.description: A Bexhill county councillor has left Reform UK and joined the Conservative Party, the party's East Sussex group has said.

item.title: Aldwick man jailed for 15 years over murder of his wife
item.description: Michael Pyke, 79, of Aldwick, has been jailed for 15 years for the murder of his wife, Sussex Police have confirmed.

item.title: Bexhill seafront kiosk owner Stella Brennan-Wright dies aged 79
item.description: A well-loved Bexhill seafront kiosk owner has died, her family has announced.

item.title: Police appeal for information over St Leonards burglary
item.description: Sussex Police are appealing for information in connection with a burglary in Eversfield Place, St Leonards.

item.title: Kray twins' biographer Fred Dinenage to speak at Hastings White Rock
item.description: Hastings White Rock is offering the chance to delve into the lives of Britain's most notorious gangsters with the Krays' official biographer, Fred Dinenage.

item.title: Update: Plans for up to 125 homes at Robertsbridge mill site
item.description: The approval is subject to conditions and the signing of a detailed legal agreement, expected to secure a 'late stage review' of the scheme's affordability, because a Financial Viability Appraisal had concluded the proposed development could not support the provision of any affordable housing.

item.title: Southwick man jailed for 12 years over £2m jewellery and gold scams
item.description: James Charles, 49, of Roman Crescent, Southwick, has been jailed for 12 years after running a major fraud operation through his companies, Sussex Police said.

item.title: Bexhill Christmas lights switch-on and market on December 5
item.description: Bexhill's Christmas lights switch-on and festive market will take place on Saturday, December 5, from 3pm to 7pm in Western Road and Devonshire Square.

item.title: Rewilding sessions help children feel calmer, Hastings project says
item.description: Children taking part in an outdoor rewilding scheme based in Hastings have described the sessions as helping them to feel calmer, according to the BBC.

item.title: On this day, 1939: A wartime RAF training wing formed at the Eversfield Hotel
item.description: On this day in 1939, No 5 Initial Training Wing of the Royal Air Force was formed at the Eversfield Hotel in Hastings, in No 54 Group.

item.title: Update: Plans for up to 125 homes at Robertsbridge mill site
item.description: Rother District Council's planning committee has approved Homes England's application for up to 125 homes at the Hodson's Mill site in Northbridge Street. The committee heard that the Salehurst and Robertsbridge parish council strongly supports the scheme, and voted to approve the application in line with officers' recommendation. Under the plans, the Grade II listed oast house is to be dismantled and rebuilt to provide two three-bedroom homes, and the mill building converted to provide two retail and community units and nine flats.

item.title: Update: Plans for up to 125 homes at Robertsbridge mill site
item.description: Rother District Council's planning committee has approved Homes England's application for up to 125 homes at the Hodson's Mill site in Northbridge Street. The committee heard that the Salehurst and Robertsbridge parish council strongly supports the scheme, and voted to approve the application in line with officers' recommendation. Under the plans, the Grade II listed oast house is to be dismantled and rebuilt to provide two three-bedroom homes, and the mill building converted to provide two retail and community units and nine flats.

item.title: Police appeal for information after St Leonards building vandalised
item.description: Police have appealed for witnesses after windows were smashed and graffiti was daubed on a building in St Leonards.

item.title: Rye man named community champion in housing association awards
item.description: Dan Lake, who lives in Tilling Green near Rye, has been named Community Champion in Southern Housing's 2026 Shine Bright Awards.

item.title: Bricks are temporary on St Clements gate pillar, church says
item.description: Concerns raised this week about a modern red brick repair to the gate pillar at St Clements Church in Hastings Old Town have been answered by the church, which said the bricks are a temporary measure.

item.title: Hastings pub to host Flying Nun record label DJ night
item.description: A DJ night celebrating the music of New Zealand's Flying Nun record label is coming to Hastings.

item.title: Health watchdog orders rapid improvements at Conquest Hospital emergency care
item.description: The Care Quality Commission has downgraded the urgent and emergency care service at the Conquest Hospital in St Leonards from 'good' to 'requires improvement' and ordered East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust to submit an action plan showing what action it is taking to make immediate improvements. The hospital's overall rating has moved from 'outstanding' to 'good'.

item.title: Police 'urgently searching' for 14-year-old girl missing from Bexhill
item.description: Sussex Police are urgently searching for a 14-year-old girl who has been missing from Bexhill since Tuesday (November 10).

item.title: Rother council to invest £1.3m in seven local projects
item.description: Rother District Council has approved £1.3m from its Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) fund to support seven projects across the district, aimed at improving local facilities, enhancing accessibility and promoting sustainability.

item.title: Hastings council rejects community asset bid for St Leonards convent site
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has turned down a bid to list the former Convent of the Holy Child Jesus on Magdalen Road, St Leonards, as an Asset of Community Value.

item.title: Former Bexhill teacher jailed for raping and sexually assaulting a child
item.description: A former teacher from Bexhill has been jailed for raping and sexually assaulting a child, Sussex Police said.

item.title: New wheelchair and mobility scooter support group launched in Hastings
item.description: A new support group for residents who use wheelchairs or mobility scooters is being launched in Hastings.

item.title: East Sussex energy group urges residents to contact MPs on heat pumps and EV targets
item.description: As the UN climate summit, COP31, begins in Turkey, the local community benefit society Energise Sussex Coast is calling on the government to restore heat pump funding, keep its current electric vehicle targets and reject the Rosebank oil field in the North Sea, according to the Hastings Online Times.

item.title: Hastings couple to mark 70th Platinum wedding anniversary
item.description: A Hastings couple is to celebrate its 70th, or Platinum, wedding anniversary next month.

item.title: On this day, 1964: This day in 1964: Kevin Ball was born in Hastings
item.description: On this day in 1964, Kevin Ball was born in Hastings. He went on to have a professional football career, according to Wikipedia, with his senior career running from 1981 to 2002 across five clubs: Coventry City, Portsmouth, Sunderland, Fulham and Burnley.

item.title: Saxon Mount School submits plans to replace mobile classrooms with two-storey building
item.description: Saxon Mount School, in Edinburgh Road, St Leonards, has submitted a planning application to replace its four single-storey mobile classrooms with a new two-storey building.

item.title: Man charged with theft after evading police across railway line at Rye
item.description: A 45-year-old man has been charged with theft after stealing alcohol worth £130 from Jempsons supermarket at Rye.

item.title: Southern services delayed between Eastbourne and Hastings after trespassers
item.description: Travellers between Eastbourne and Hastings faced delays on Wednesday afternoon after trespassers were found on the railway.

item.title: Liane Carroll to give Christmas concert at St Clement's for the Sara Lee Trust
item.description: Award-winning jazz artist Liane Carroll is to give a Christmas concert in Hastings to raise vital funds for the Sara Lee Trust, the local cancer charity.

item.title: Hastings MP marks one-year anniversary of the beach 'beads' pollution incident
item.description: It is a year since Southern Water admitted responsibility for the millions of plastic beads that washed up on the beaches at Hastings, Camber Sands and at Rye Harbour Nature Reserve, and Hastings MP Helena Dollimore has marked the anniversary of what is thought to be one of the biggest plastic pollution incidents on the South Coast of England.

item.title: Police seek man over theft of cash from Bexhill M&S
item.description: Sussex Police is seeking a man in connection with the theft of cash from the Marks and Spencer store in Ravenside Retail Park, Bexhill.

item.title: Rye Town Clerk honoured with the town's highest civic award
item.description: Richard Farhall has been made an Honorary Freeman of the Ancient Town of Rye, the town's highest civic award, in recognition of his 26 years of service as Rye Town Clerk.

item.title: St Leonards Frost Fair returns on November 28 with Snow Queen parade
item.description: The St Leonards Frost Fair returns on Saturday 28 November with a parade of colourful fairy-tale characters, led by the Snow Queen, processing through the streets.

item.title: Two Bexhill Colonnade kiosks available to let for new businesses
item.description: Two kiosks at the Grade II listed Colonnade in Bexhill are available to let for new businesses, offered through commercial property agents Dyer & Hobbis.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Hastings council budgets £1,937,861 for St Mary in the Castle in 2026/27
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has budgeted spending of £1,937,861 on the Grade II* listed seafront building St Mary in the Castle in the 2026/27 financial year, with the majority set to come forward as capital spending.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Two men charged with murder of Bexhill cyclist
item.description: Two men have appeared at Lewes Crown Court, charged with the murder of a Bexhill cyclist, Sussex Police have said.

item.title: Councillor calls 500-home Bexhill plan a 'disaster zone waiting to happen'
item.description: A Bexhill town councillor has described proposals for a potential 500 new homes in the town as a 'disaster zone waiting to happen'.

item.title: Donations top £10,000 for Isfield farm shop after raid
item.description: Donations totalling more than £10,000 have flowed in to help a family farm in Isfield after thieves ransacked its shop, the owners said.

item.title: On this day, 1918: The Armistice reaches the East Sussex papers, 1918
item.description: When news of the Armistice reached Britain on 11 November 1918, newspapers in East Sussex reported on the joy and the solemn reflection of the county.

item.title: Residents to have say on East Sussex supported housing strategy
item.description: People in supported housing across the district can have their say on how it should improve, Rother District Council has said.

item.title: Bexhill Leisure Centre named UK Active Awards finalist
item.description: Bexhill Leisure Centre has been named a finalist for Regional Centre of the Year at the UK Active Awards, one of the leisure industry's leading national award programmes.

item.title: Little Common Library marks annual volunteer lunch
item.description: Volunteers and supporters came together in Bexhill for Little Common Library's annual fish and chip lunch, its chairman Connor Winter said.

item.title: Plans for 42 new homes by St Leonards' Bannatyne's Spa Hotel
item.description: Outline permission has been submitted to build up to 42 homes on land at Bannatyne's Spa Hotel in Hastings Road, St Leonards, according to the latest Hastings Borough Council planning applications.

item.title: Battle Bonfire 2026: 'Guy Feaux' effigy takes a swipe at AI
item.description: Battle High Street became a 'river of fire' on Saturday night as people turned out for the town's annual bonfire celebrations, the Hastings Observer reported.

item.title: Nineteen-year-old opens her own beauty salon in Bexhill
item.description: Grace Guenigault, 19, has opened her own beauty salon in Bexhill, the Hastings Observer reported.

item.title: Rye Bonfire named among the UK's best Bonfire Night displays
item.description: The Rye and District Bonfire has been named among the best Bonfire Night displays in the country, The Argus reports.

item.title: Hastings brothers set for Nepal peaks for veterans' charity
item.description: Two brothers from Hastings are heading to the Himalayas to raise money for a local veterans' charity.

item.title: Westfield player Michael Rwabigwi called up for Rwanda
item.description: A player at a tenth-tier English football club has been called up to represent his country.

item.title: On this day, 1883: Electric street lights trial switched on in Hastings
item.description: This week in November 1883, a trial of electric street lights in the town was switched on.

item.title: Police launch manhunt for man wanted for recall to prison
item.description: Police have launched a manhunt for a man wanted for recall to prison and are asking anyone who sees him to call 999.

item.title: St Leonards' Becky Palmer wins Christmas tree flinging at Catsfield
item.description: A 27-year-old from St Leonards has won the women's title at the Christmas tree flinging contest at Catsfield Christmas Tree Farm near Battle.

item.title: Two Sussex police officers charged over assault of detained man
item.description: Two Sussex Police officers have been charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm over an incident involving a man detained in hospital under the Mental Health Act, according to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

item.title: Swansea Sound to open tour at The Piper in St Leonards
item.description: Swansea Sound, who feature members of Heavenly and Talulah Gosh, are to kick off their tour in St Leonards at The Piper on 13 November.

item.title: Camber Sands holiday park ranked among worst in UK
item.description: Camber Sands Holiday Park, near Rye, has been named one of the lowest-rated holiday parks in the country.

item.title: St Leonards and Hastings properties sell at Clive Emson auction
item.description: A mixed-use property at 32 Kings Road, St Leonards, has been sold before the auction in one of the latest Clive Emson Auctioneers sales, which listed 174 lots across southern England.

item.title: Local band raises £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless
item.description: A group of local musicians have raised around £3,000 for Warming Up the Homeless in the last couple of years by giving their CDs away free and encouraging audiences to donate to the charity instead.
